papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) requires accurate subtyping for prognosis and treatment, yet conventional histopathology is time-consuming and subjective. This study applies label-free multiphoton microscopy (MPM) to quantify extracellular matrix remodeling, imaging collagen via SHG and elastin via TPEF in 88 specimens from 72 patients. We introduce a SHG/TPEF ratio (STR) system to assess tumor invasiveness. Results show progressive "fiber desertification," reduced fiber content, and decreased collagen alignment in high-grade LUAD subtypes. STR metrics strongly correlate with pathological grading and effectively distinguish aggressive patterns. This MPM-based framework enables rapid, objective intraoperative identification of high-grade LUAD, improving diagnostic precision and clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: Longer Barrett esophagus (BE) segments are associated with worse outcomes than shorter segments. However, it remains uncertain whether BE length is still a clinically actionable variable in modern surveillance, risk stratification, and treatment pathways. We reviewed current literature on the relevance of BE length as a predictor of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) severity, cancer risk, treatment outcomes, regression after treatment, and remission after ablation. BE length correlates with hiatal hernia size, esophageal dysmotility, esophagitis, and acid exposure time. Long-segment BE carries a greater risk of dysplasia or progression to esophageal adenocarcinoma than short-segment BE, although smaller segments are not risk-free. Longer BE length was associated with treatment failure and increased post-treatment pain. BE length also predicted recurrence of BE, dysplasia, or adenocarcinoma after endoscopic ablation therapy. In conclusion, most current studies report BE outcomes without stratifying results by length. BE length, however, functions as a continuous clinical variable that influences multiple aspects of care, including progression risk, surveillance intervals, treatment complexity, likelihood of eradication, recurrence after therapy, and incorporation into emerging prediction models. In other words, the contemporary importance of length lies less in preserving a historical cutoff than in recognizing length as one component of multidimensional risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an aggressive malignancy with dismal clinical outcomes, and how cellular senescence modulates ESCC biology remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomic profiles from the TCGA-ESCC cohort with a curated panel of cellular senescence-related genes to identify and functionally validate senescence-associated regulators in ESCC. Univariate Cox regression and consensus clustering stratified ESCC patients into two molecular subtypes with divergent survival. Through differential expression analysis, random forest prioritization, and independent validation in the GSE20347 cohort, we identified GREM2 and PIK3C2G as lead candidate genes. Both were consistently downregulated in ESCC tumors and cell lines, and low expression predicted poorer overall survival. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments demonstrated that GREM2 and PIK3C2G drive p16/p21-dependent cellular senescence, trigger the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), and restrict proliferation in esophageal epithelial cells. Immune correlation analyses linked both genes to immune cell infiltration, chemokine signaling, and MHC molecule expression in the tumor microenvironment. These findings establish GREM2 and PIK3C2G as senescence-associated tumor suppressors in ESCC, offering candidate biomarkers and a rationale for exploring senescence-directed therapies in this disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Targeted therapy improves survival of oncogene-driven NSCLC. We evaluate the clinical outcome of advanced NSCLC with oncogenic drivers in LC-SCRUM-Asia Taiwanese and Japanese cohort using tiered groups of disease-driven oncogene. METHODS: Fourteen genes were reported from NGS and grouped into four tiers based on lines of approved targeted therapies in Taiwan and Japan (Tier 1: ≥ two lines; Tier 2: one line; Tier 3: not targetable; Tier 4: potentially targetable; not yet approved). Overall survival (OS) of the four-tier gene groups was analyzed in Taiwanese cohort and validated in the 8619 Japanese patients using a two-stage approach. RESULTS: Three-hundred-fifty-nine patients were enrolled in Taiwanese cohort, of which 249 (69.4%) patients had a reported genomic alteration. Patients with a history of smoking (HR 0.46 [95% CI, 0.23-0.92]; p=0.031) and squamous cell carcinoma (HR 0.31 [95% CI, 0.12-0.78]; p=0.014) had a lower incidence of genomic alterations. The top five genomic alterations were EGFR (44.6%), KRAS (7.2%), ALK (3.9%), MET (3.1%) and ERBB2 (2.5%) mutations. The four-tier gene groups were significantly associated with different OS in Taiwanese patients (Log rank test p < 0.001). The adjusted OS was the longest and the shortest in patients with Tier 1 (34.5 months) and Tier 4 (16.6 months) gene groups, respectively. In Japanese cohort, a similar trend between the four-tier gene groups and OS was observed (Log rank test p < 0.001) where the Tier 1 and the Tier 4 gene groups also demonstrated the longest (42.6 months) and the shortest OS (18.9 months), respectively. CONCLUSION: The available lines of targeted therapy impact survival in patients of advanced oncogene-driven NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) can show declining age-standardized rates while the number of affected people grows. We quantified this divergence and its demographic and socioeconomic pattern across Asia. METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates for 48 Asian locations (2009-2023), primary analyses examined incidence, prevalence, deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), age-sex patterns, estimated annual percentage changes, demographic decomposition, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI)-related inequality. Exploratory analyses assessed pre-2020 trend deviations and subregional ARIMA forecasts to 2030. RESULTS: From 2009 to 2023, incident cases increased from 7.74 million to 10.75 million (38.9%), prevalent cases from 91.88 million to 129.76 million (41.2%), deaths from 2.11 million to 2.63 million (24.8%), and DALYs from 46.43 million to 55.97 million (20.5%). Age-standardized incidence and prevalence rates declined in 34 of 48 locations, death rates in 37, and DALY rates in 43. Of 522,061 additional deaths, population growth contributed 345,084 and population aging 933,776, partly offset by epidemiological change (-756,799). The death-rate SII changed from -69.90 in 2009 to -87.22 in 2023, and the concentration index from -0.140 to -0.220, indicating increasing concentration in lower-SDI populations. Summed subregional point deviations for 2020-2023 were small relative to expected burden: deaths were 0.57% and DALYs 0.26% above expected, whereas incidence was 0.35% and prevalence 0.51% below expected. Conditional 2030 point forecasts were 13.28 million incident cases, 156.74 million prevalent cases, 2.81 million deaths, and 62.63 million DALYs. CONCLUSION: Declining age-standardized rates have not reduced COPD service need across Asia. Population aging and lower-SDI disadvantage support prevention and care strategies tailored to demographic and socioeconomic context.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Pulmonary vascular involvement is a determinant of worse outcomes in fibrotic lung diseases. Its prevalence and prognostic relevance in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is unknown. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of indirect echocardiographic abnormalities in progressive pulmonary fibrosis before antifibrotic therapy, characterize a baseline high-risk cardiopulmonary functional profile, and assess 12-month clinical trajectories. METHODS: Observational, retrospective, multicentre study. RESULTS: 158 patients (median (IQR) age of 71 (65.2-77.0) years) with PPF were enrolled. Thirty (19.0%) had ≥ 1 echocardiographic indirect sign of increased right-sided afterload, 15 (9.5%) ≥ 2, 9 (5.7%) ≥ 3 and 1 (0.6%) all four. A shortened right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (< 105 ms) was the most frequent alteration (12.7%), followed by right atrial dilation (10.8%). In univariable analysis, ≥1 sign was associated with male sex, a lower DLCO% predicted, a higher FVC%/DLCO% ratio and a shorter 6MWD; in the multivariable model only, male sex remained independently associated (aOR 3.45, 95% CI 0.99-12.07; p = 0.052). Twelve-month FVC trajectories did not differ by baseline echocardiographic status; nonetheless, ≥1 sign was associated with shorter time to acute exacerbation (log-rank p = 0.007) and all-cause hospitalisation (p = 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic signs suggestive of increased right-sided afterload are present in a substantial proportion of PPF patients at the time of antifibrotic initiation. They identified patients at higher risk of acute exacerbation and hospitalisation, regardless of FVC decline. This higher-risk subgroup warrants specific pulmonary vascular evaluation and tighter clinical follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: IntroductionLung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Alabama, where screening uptake remains well below national benchmarks. Decentralized screening programs, in which referring providers manage eligibility identification, referrals, and follow-up without dedicated coordination infrastructure, are common across clinical settings. Yet the relationship between program design and delivery outcomes in decentralized contexts has received little attention. This study examined how a decentralized lung cancer screening program delivered screening across each step of the pathway, from patient identification through annual follow-up. The goal was to identify where and how program design produced gaps in delivery from the perspectives of patients and providers.MethodsThis qualitative study used semi-structured interviews conducted between July 2023 and May 2024 at an academic medical center in Alabama as part of a larger explanatory sequential mixed methods study. Fifteen patients who had completed screening and six providers representing primary care, pulmonology, and radiology participated. Interviews explored screening awareness, decision-making, and program delivery processes. Transcripts were analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and constant comparative method. Reporting followed the COREQ guideline.ResultsDelivery failures were structural and concentrated at the front end of the screening pathway. Eligibility identification depended on incidental patient exposure rather than systematic outreach. Referrals reflected individual provider initiative rather than standardized workflows. Result tracking and nodule follow-up fell to ordering providers without dedicated support. Coverage gaps and geographic distance compounded these determinants.ConclusionReduced uptake in this decentralized program pointed largely to structural barriers. Closing the implementation gap may require program design changes and proactive outreach that does not depend on the clinical encounter to begin.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) incidence is rising globally, and current therapeutic options carry substantial morbidity and mortality. We report the feasibility and early outcomes of knife-assisted endoscopic full-thickness resection (kFTR) as a palliative local control in nonsurgical candidates. METHODS: Three patients with suspected locally advanced distal EAC (clinical tumor stage T1b-T2), no nodal or distant disease, and high Charlson Comorbidity Index scores were unfit for surgery and declined chemoradiotherapy. All consented to kFTR: a submucosal pocket was created cranial to the suspected invasive area, the muscle-retracting sign was identified, and the muscularis propria was incised to access the periesophageal space. The lesion was dissected laterally and resected en bloc. A fully covered metal stent was then placed. RESULTS: Patients resumed oral intake on day 5 without major adverse events. All had EAC pathologic tumor stage 1b with invasion into the deepest layer of the submucosa; 2 had positive vertical margins. One remained disease-free (24 months); 2 had local recurrence by 6 months but remained asymptomatic at last follow-up (10 and 14 months). CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected symptomatic, inoperable patients, kFTR achieved short-to-medium term symptom control for locally advanced EAC with acceptable safety.

papers.abstract_en: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, immune-mediated disease whose incidence and prevalence have continued to rise, yet little is known about how public awareness has evolved alongside clinical progress. We used Google Trends, a freely available tool that indexes the relative popularity of search queries from 0 to 100, to examine interest in the terms 'eosinophilic esophagitis' and 'EoE' in the United States from January 2004 through December 2025, and to compare the disease term with searches for regulatory-approved EoE-relevant therapies (dupilumab/Dupixent, budesonide/Eohilia, and budesonide/Jorveza) in the United States and worldwide (English-language). Search interest for 'eosinophilic esophagitis' rose substantially across two decades (+2.97 points/year; P < 0.001), with segmented regression at clinical milestones showing significant slope changes at 2007, 2011, 2013, 2020, and 2024 (all P ≤ 0.04). Secondary analysis of the 'EoE' acronym corroborated these patterns, rising across the study period (+1.3 points/year; P < 0.001) with a final-year rise (+18.2 points/year). Searches for 'Dupixent' exceeded disease-term searches in both the United States and worldwide (English-language). Seasonal and monthly variation did not statistically differ. These observations illustrate how digital epidemiology has potential to serve as a low-cost barometer of disease awareness and information-seeking behavior. As patients increasingly turn from search engines to conversational artificial intelligence, these signals may evolve and further research is needed to define how digital epidemiology best be integrated with conventional epidemiologic data.
